title: Boston, Plotted | Michael and Allie

header.eyebrow: Plotted course · Fri Jul 24 to Sun Jul 26, 2026
header.sub: A daddy daughter weekend on foot and on the water. Home port: Hyatt Place Seaport District. Just the harbor, the neighborhoods, and the food.

facts.html: Land 10:20 AM Fri · UA641 · Term B ↗
Fly out 7:24 PM Sun · UA2136 · Term B ↗

days.heading: Day 1 · Friday, July 24
days.course: Land, cross the harbor, and settle into the Seaport. Downtown, the Greenway, and dinner in the North End.

legs.titleHtml: Land at Logan, cross the harbor by water taxi
legs.bodyHtml: Step by step: (1) UA641 lands at Terminal B; you're carry-on only, so skip baggage claim entirely and follow signs straight out to Arrivals, Level 1. (2) Walk out to the arrivals curb and board the free Route 66 shuttle; it loops every terminal and ends at the Logan Boat Dock, 5 to 10 minutes. (3) At the dock, call or app-summon an on-demand water taxi (signage at the dock has the operators; boats usually arrive within 10 to 15 minutes, about $20 per person). (4) Tell the captain Fan Pier. Ten minutes across the harbor, skyline the whole way. (5) From the Fan Pier dock, walk 6 minutes: away from the water to Northern Ave, turn left, Hyatt Placesite is at 295.

chips.label: Shuttle + water taxi + walk · about 35 min, no bag wait

legs.tipHtml: Allie's first view of Boston is from the water.

swap.label: Bad weather backup
swap.bodyHtml: Silver Line SL1 bus, curbside at every terminal's arrivals level, free heading into the city, every 10 min. Ride it through the harbor tunnel to the first stop, Silver Line Way, then walk 5 min to the hotel.

legs.titleHtml: Drop bags at Hyatt Place Seaport
legs.bodyHtml: Room likely won't be ready, but they'll hold your luggage. Change into walking shoes — it's a lot of walking today.
Bill Barrett's pick, a five-minute walk on Fort Point Channel. Picnic tables under the tent — crab legs, lobster roll, and the chowder Song recommended. Casual and loud.

swap.label: Swap
swap.bodyHtml: James Hook & Cosite next door for a faster counter service lobster roll if the Crab has a wait.

legs.bodyHtml: Cross the Seaport Boulevard bridge and follow the Harborwalk north along the water past the aquariumsite to Long Wharf. Jeff Behrens's pick — it stays on the water, with good photo stops the whole way.

legs.titleHtml: Faneuil Hall + Quincy Market, quick pass
legs.bodyHtml: Todd's pick. Street performers and the long market hall; grab a drink. It's touristy, so keep it to a 45-minute walk-through.

legs.titleHtml: Rose Kennedy Greenway to the North End
legs.bodyHtml: Walk north through the Greenway's gardens and public art, then into the North End's narrow streets. Hanover and Salem Streets are the main ones; the side streets are quieter. It's the old Italian neighborhood.
legs.tipHtml: Cannoli at Modern Pastrysite on Hanover. Megan prefers Modern over Mike'ssite. Cash speeds up the line.

legs.bodyHtml: You're already up here, so skip the trek back to the hotel. Grab an espresso and a cannoli or gelato, take a café table or a bench, and let the afternoon settle before dinner. Caffe Vittoria on Hanover is a classic place to sit. You'll check in properly tonight, on the walk back.

chips.label: Walk · you're already in the neighborhood

legs.bodyHtml: Megan's pick: red-sauce Italian with outdoor tables she flagged. Chicken parm, and a Shirley Temple for Allie.

swap.label: Swap
swap.bodyHtml: Massiminossite on Endicott St, Rob Weinhold's pick, quieter and old-school. Beth seconded it.

legs.map: Tony and Elaine's 111 N Washington St Boston

legs.titleHtml: Evening stroll: Christopher Columbus Park + waterfront lights
legs.bodyHtml: Walk off dinner under the trellis at the waterfront park, then follow the lit Harborwalk home. If you're still up for it, the Adirondack swings at The Lawn on Dsite near the hotel are lit up at night.

days.heading: Day 2 · Saturday, July 25
days.course: Beacon Hill and Back Bay in the morning, the harbor islands in the afternoon, dinner and a skyline view to finish.

legs.bodyHtml: Ride the T into town for shakshuka and a halva latte at the Charles Street Tatte. It's right at the foot of Beacon Hill.

chips.label: SL1/SL2 · Silver Line Way to South Station
Red Line · South Station to Charles/MGH

legs.bodyHtml: Gas lamps and brick sidewalks. Go to Acorn Street early, before the crowds — one of the most photographed streets in the country. Beth suggested it, and Jeffrey O'Neill seconded the neighborhood.

chips.label: Walk · the hill is the activity

legs.bodyHtml: Cross Charles Street into the Public Garden. The swan boats are about $5 and have run since 1877. The Make Way for Ducklings statues are on the way out.
Sharon's daughter loved Back Bay; Allie probably will too. Eight blocks of shops from Arlington to Mass Ave — plan to browse. Beth flagged that it may not be your favorite part, but it's Allie's day.

chips.label: Walk · Newbury runs parallel to the Garden

legs.tipHtml: Two-minute detour at Copley: the Boston Public Librarysite courtyard — free and open to the public.

legs.bodyHtml: Somewhere easy and outdoors: Stephanie's on Newburysite for the patio, or Faccia a Facciasite for a nicer room. Allie's call.

legs.titleHtml: Ferry to Georges Island, Boston Harbor Islands
legs.bodyHtml: Robert Nagle's suggestion: the harbor over the Freedom Trail. Take the T back to Long Wharf and catch the harbor-islands ferry to Georges Islandsite. Fort Warrensite is a Civil War–era granite fort with tunnels, ramparts, and skyline views back to the city.

chips.label: Green Line · Copley to Government Center, then 8-min walk to Long Wharf

legs.tipHtml: Outbound Georges Island boats are limited — roughly 10am, noon, and 2pm — so this is tight after a 1:00 lunch; confirm the 2026 schedule, and if it doesn't line up, the whale watch below has more departures. Check the return times when you land and aim for a boat back around 5:00 to 5:30.

swap.label: Swap
swap.bodyHtml: A 2-to-3-hour afternoon whale watch from Long Wharf if you'd rather do that than the fort. It books out on summer Saturdays, so decide by Thursday.

legs.bodyHtml: Allie's swap — you already have a Barcelona near home, so go for the Boston original. Toro is Ken Oringer's Spanish tapas spot in the South End. Order a few things to share: the maíz asado (grilled corn with lime, aioli, and aged cheese), patatas bravas, gambas al ajillo, and jamón.

Lien's suggestion. It's about a 20-minute walk (or a quick rideshare) from the South End to the Prudential Towersite; ride to the 52nd floor for sunset, harbor to the Charles. Sunset is about 8:10, so book the 8:00 window.

chips.label: Walk · 20 min, or a short rideshare

legs.tipHtml: On the walk over, pass the Christian Science Plaza reflecting pool — it mirrors the skyline at dusk.

days.heading: Day 3 · Sunday, July 26
days.course: The Duck Tour, dim sum in Chinatown, a last lap of the harbor, then Logan.

legs.bodyHtml: Joanne Chang's original location. Split the well-known sticky bun and get real breakfast too. Seven-minute walk from the hotel.

Recommended by Jeffrey, Megan, and Adrian. It departs from and returns to the Prudential Center (Huntington Ave side)site — about 80 minutes through the city in a WWII-style amphibious vehicle that drives straight into the Charles River. Expect some audience participation. Back at the Pru just before noon.
legs.tipHtml: Ask to sit near the front for the river entry splash.

legs.titleHtml: Lunch: Sunday dim sum in Chinatown
legs.bodyHtml: Vaibhav suggested Chinatown, and Sunday is the best day for dim sum. About a 20-minute walk from the Duck Tour drop-off, or a couple of Green Line stops. China Pearlsite for cart dim sum, or Gourmet Dumpling House for soup dumplings. Grab bubble tea on the way out.

legs.titleHtml: Greenway back, with an optional final cannoli
legs.bodyHtml: Exit through the Chinatown Gate onto the Rose Kennedy Greenway and walk north one last time — fountains, a carousel, public art. If Friday's Modern Pastrysite was a hit, the North End is ten minutes further for a boxed half-dozen to take home.
Back to the Seaport for a slow lap of the Harborwalk at Fan Pier, the Adirondack swings at The Lawn on Dsite, or a coffee by the water. This block is left open on purpose.

chips.label: Walk · ~30 min from North End, ~25 from Chinatown, or a water taxi

legs.bodyHtml: Grab luggage from the bell desk, water bottles filled, boarding passes on your phones.

legs.titleHtml: Cross back to Logan the way you came
legs.bodyHtml: Reverse Friday: (1) 4:15, walk 6 minutes from the hotel to the Fan Pier dock; call the water taxi 15 minutes ahead so the boat is waiting. (2) Ten minute crossing to the Logan Boat Dock. (3) Board the free Route 66 shuttle at the dock and hop off at the Terminal B sign; carry-on only with mobile boarding passes, so walk straight past check-in to security. (4) You're at security around 4:50, a full 2.5 hours before UA2136's 7:24 departure. Since Logan is new to you, that's a comfortable cushion for security, with time for dinner after.

chips.label: Walk + water taxi + shuttle · about 35 min door to terminal

swap.label: Backup
swap.bodyHtml: SL1 from Silver Line Way runs direct to every terminal, about 25 min. Fares run one way here: free coming from Logan, standard $2.40 fare going to it. Tap a contactless card or phone when boarding.

Tony & Elaine's, Friday 6:45 PM · ask for outdoor seating. Reserve › Call
Harbor Islands ferry, Saturday afternoon · round trip to Georges Island, or swap to a whale watch and book that instead. Ferry tickets ›
Water taxi on demand · Boston Harbor water taxis run on call when you land. Call 617-406-8584 Get the app ›
checklist.notes: Good to know: Late July is warm and humid, so the harbor legs help. Allie is 20, so everything here is all-ages — restaurants, not bars. Sunday is padded on purpose: at Logan by ~4:50 for a 7:24 flight, since it's your first time there. Checkout is likely noon, so leave bags with the bell desk Sunday morning before the Duck Tour. Everything is walk, boat, or one T ride.

packing.heading: Pack light — carry-on only
packing.lede: Two bags, no checked luggage. Tap to pack.
items: Broken-in walking shoes — you two will log 15k+ steps a day
Light layers + a packable rain shell for the harbor breeze
Sunglasses, a hat, and sunscreen (July sun bounces off the water)
Portable battery pack + charging cables
Refillable water bottle each
Any meds, plus a few blister bandages — moleskin saves the trip
IDs and a card or two; boarding passes saved on your phones
A packable tote for Newbury St finds and a boxed half-dozen cannoli
One nicer outfit each for dinners (Tony & Elaine's, Barcelona)

optional.heading: Optional add-ons
optional.lede: A couple of extra ideas — with my honest take on each.

cards.map: Boston Tea Party Ships and Museum 306 Congress St Boston
cards.bodyHtml: A non-art option close to the hotel, on Fort Point Channel — a 10-minute walk from the hotel, near the Barking Crab. It's a guided, hands-on hour: costumed reenactors, restored tall ships, and you throw a crate of tea into the harbor. Tours run about an hour, 10am to 5pm.
cards.tipHtml: Buy timed tickets online to skip the booth line — tours leave on the hour and can sell out midday in summer.
cards.verdictHtml: My take · A good fit if you want a museum — about an hour, and it slots into Sunday's open harbor block or a rainy stretch without cutting anything. For something bigger, the free USS Constitution Museum in Charlestown pairs with a harbor ferry, and the Museum of Science is a half-day on its own.

cards.bodyHtml: Take the Red Line from Park Street or South Station straight to Harvard (about 20 minutes). Walk into Harvard Yard, rub the toe of the John Harvard statue for the photo, then duck into the Harvard Coopsite for a crimson hoodie. Wander Harvard Square — bookstores, buskers, and cafés — and grab burgers at Mr. Bartley'ssite, right across from the Yard. Time permitting, stroll to the Charles River. Red Line back — budget 3 to 4 hours door to door.

chips.label: Red Line · Park St to Harvard, about 20 min

cards.tipHtml: The free student-led Harvard Yard tour is good but needs advance sign-up and caps at five people — otherwise grab Harvard's free self-guided-tour app and go at your own pace.
cards.verdictHtml: My take · Better as a swap than an add-on — the weekend is already full. If Allie wants to see the campus, or Saturday's harbor-islands weather turns, trade the Georges Island ferry for this. Otherwise I'd keep the harbor.
